To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Ca2+ entry pathways in SH-SY cells are: 1) an agonist-dependent, voltage-sensitive, Ca2+-selective channel; 2) an agonist-independent, non-selective cation channel; and 3) a Ca2+ entry mechanism activated by store depletion.
the agonist-independent pathway in SH-SY cells is sensitive to La3+ and SKF 96365 and is activated by Ca2+ store emptying.
Ca2+ entry into neuroblastoma cells following depletion of internal Ca2+ stores is not dependent upon the release of agonists from internal stores.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which Ca2+ enters neurons and how it is involved in the release of neurotransmitter.
the mechanisms by which Ca2+ enters cells following depletion of intracellular stores.
the mechanisms underlying Ca(2+)-dependent neurotransmitter release in neuroendocrine cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ca2+ entry is a complex process involving multiple pathways and the present work has provided a detailed description of one of these pathways.
Ca2+ entry through a store-operated pathway is mediated through the release of Ca2+.
Ca2+ entry is a process that is activated by the depletion of Ca2+ stores and is mediated by the influx of Ca2+ across the plasma membrane through a non-selective cation channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the store-operated Ca2+ entry in SH-SY cells is mediated by a non-selective cation channel.
the store-operated Ca2+ entry in SH-SY 5Y cells is mediated by a receptor-operated channel.
the Ca2+ entry pathways activated by store depletion in SH SY5Y cells are not sensitive to agonists, but are sensitive to the La3+ and SKF 96365 and are permeable to Ca2+, Mn2+, Sr 2+ and Ba 2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the store depletion-induced Ca2+ entry in SH-SY cells is a novel pathway, distinct from other known pathways, which may be important for neuronal signaling.
the SH-SY5y cells express a Ca2+ entry current activated by store depletion that is insensitive to the muscarinic M3 receptor agonist.
store depletion activates a pathway that is distinct from the Ca2+ entry pathways that are activated by receptor stimulation.
